content.jointProblem: Can TloCare and the researcher develop and test a spatial prediction and adaptive-sampling workflow that uses existing soil sampling records and available covariates to identify sub-hectare salinity pockets near the Tisa before field teams are sent? The first experiment would test whether such a model can prioritise denser sampling only where salinity risk is high, without promising accuracy before validation.

rationale.text: Filipović has directly characterised field-scale spatial variability of ESP and ECe in Vojvodina solonetz, including salinity hotspots in micro-depressions that resemble the pockets TloCare is missing.

sources.quote: Hotspots of ESP > 25% occupied 18% of the surveyed area, concentrated in micro-depressions with restricted drainage.

rationale.text: He has used EM induction surveys calibrated against laboratory ECe to produce salinisation-class maps, which is a proximal-sensing route for guiding sampling where early vegetation indices are weak.

sources.quote: EM38 and EM31 electromagnetic induction instruments were used to map apparent soil electrical conductivity (ECa) across 2,300 ha
Predicted ECe maps delineated three salinisation classes covering 8%, 31%, and 61% of the area.

rationale.text: He has built machine-learning classifiers from Sentinel-2, EM38 and soil-map covariates to screen parcels, which is directly relevant to predicting variable zones before sending field teams.

sources.quote: Random forest and gradient boosting classifiers were trained to predict whether individual 1-ha parcels in the Bačka lowland met agronomic criteria for immediate reclamation

rationale.text: His SALTMOD calibration at Bečej and Novi Bečej gives local salt-balance modelling capacity for the Tisa-area landscapes named in the task.

sources.quote: calibrated and validated for two contrasting solonetz sites in Vojvodina (Bečej and Novi Bečej districts)

risks: Transfer gap: the geostatistical, EM induction and machine-learning evidence comes from Bačka or Tamiš–Bega datasets, not from the Tisa floodplain parcels named by TloCare; the first experiment must hold out Tisa parcels and compare predictions against denser sampling.
The historical 18,000 points were collected on a 4-ha grid and may be too sparse to label 0.3–0.8 ha salinity pockets; validation may require new dense sampling at targeted sites.
Single-depth sampling protocols can underestimate subsurface alkalisation extent by 30–40%, so a surface-only prediction may miss depth-dependent salinity.
The researcher's availability and industrial PhD willingness are unknown; administrative load above his stated tolerance could stall the collaboration.
TloCare has not yet confirmed which field sensor it will introduce, so sensor choice and data quality remain unresolved.
questions: Confirm that both sides intend a joint project, and clarify whether industrial PhD supervision is also of interest; the researcher's industrial PhD willingness and availability are currently unknown.
Can TloCare provide a clear data-sharing agreement covering the 18,000 historical GPS/lab records and client parcel data before work starts?
Which Tisa-area parcels, such as Ravnica Agro near Novi Bečej, can be densely sampled as validation sites, and what budget and time are available for that validation?
Which field sensor route is planned first, electrical conductivity or near-infrared spectroscopy, and when would it become available?
What spatial resolution and prediction accuracy must be reached before the workflow is allowed to guide field sampling?
Can the project keep administrative work below 20% of the researcher's time and confirm the company's one-third developer/GIS capacity?
